assumptions: The callees other than the trim (0x5f6b660, 0x5f79580, 0x5f870a0, 0x5f9c7b0, 0x5f801f0, 0x5f6bc90, 0x5f6d700, 0x5f880b0) are recorded as call steps with their argument registers, not modelled; their own semantics are not claimed here.
The tail-jump site 0x5f8857c is recorded as a site only; the containing wrapper function is not modelled here.
A group entry whose begin pointer is past its end pointer is not empty to the native code; the model follows the native equality test exactly.
The native code reads memory without checks; the model raises PipelineTrimError for a short group list, an out-of-range count, or a missing entry instead.

0x5f6bc55.rule: index == -1 after stepping -> return with +0x14 holding 0

0x5f6bc5e.rule: entry begin == entry end -> empty arm: store index, step to previous entry

0x5f8851f.rule: flag byte at arg2+0x193 == 0 -> fall through to the 0x5f6d700 call

0x5f88528.rule: flag byte at arg2+0x193 != 0 -> tail-jump to 0x5f880b0 at once

fields.group_entries: obj+0xa98, 24-byte records (begin, end, third qword never read)

semantics.pipeline: call order above, with the trimmed count read back from +0x14 as the third argument of the 0x5f9c7b0 call and the arg2+0x193 flag byte selecting the final path
semantics.trim: store count to +0x14; if count <= 0 return; else scan entries from the last downward, storing each empty entry's index to +0x14, stopping at the first non-empty entry or after storing 0 for an all-empty list
